q: 1. Maximum bending moment in a beam occurs where
explain: Since dM/dx = Shear Force, the bending moment is maximum (or minimum) where the shear force is zero, i.e. where the SF diagram changes sign.

q: 2. Rate of change of bending moment is equal to
explain: From beam theory, dM/dx = V (Shear Force); hence rate of change of bending moment along the span equals the shear force at that section.

q: 3. The diagram showing the variation of axial load along the span is called
explain: A thrust diagram specifically plots the variation of axial (normal) force/thrust along the length of a member, as distinct from shear force or bending moment diagrams.

q: 4. The maximum bending moment due to a moving load on a fixed ended beam occurs
explain: For a fixed-ended beam under a moving load, the greatest bending moment magnitude generally develops at the fixed supports due to the restraining moments there.

q: 5. The product EI is called
explain: The product of Young's modulus (E) and Moment of Inertia (I) defines the bending resistance of a beam, known as flexural rigidity.

q: 6. In a continuous bending moment curve he point where it changes sign, is called
explain: All three terms — point of inflexion, point of contraflexure, and point of virtual hinge — refer to the same location where the bending moment changes sign (crosses zero).

q: 7. Along the neutral axis of a simply supported beam
explain: By definition, the neutral axis is the layer in a beam where bending-induced longitudinal strain is zero — fibres there neither stretch nor compress.

q: 8. Stress in a beam due to simple bending is
explain: Bending stress is directly proportional to the distance from the neutral axis (y).

q: 9. A simply supported beam which carries a uniformly distributed load has two equal overhangs. To have maximum B.M. produced in the beam least possible, the ratio of length of the overhang to the total length of the beam is
explain: For a beam with equal overhangs under UDL, equating the numerically equal midspan sagging moment and overhang hogging moment gives an optimum overhang ratio of approximately 0.207 (i.e., 0.5(√2 − 1) of the span between supports).

q: 10. The point of contraflexure is the point where
explain: By definition, the point of contraflexure is where the bending moment diagram crosses zero, i.e. where the bending moment changes sign from sagging to hogging or vice versa.

q: 11. The amount of temperature stress is .......... in fixed beam if compared with propped cantilever.
explain: A fixed beam provides total constraint at both ends, whereas a propped cantilever may allow some relief of stress depending on the specific support conditions and degrees of freedom.

q: 12. A simply supported uniform rectangular bar breadth b, depth d and length L, carries an isolated load W at its mid span. The same bar experiences an extension e under same tensile load. The ratio of the maximum deflection to the elongation is
explain: Comparing the standard bending deflection formula (WL³/48EI) to the axial elongation formula (WL/AE) for the same bar and load leads to a ratio proportional to (L/2d)², as given in option (c); note options c and d are printed identically in the source book.

q: 13. The deflection of a uniform circular bar of diameter d and length l, which extends by an amount e under a tensile pull W, when it carries the same load at its mid span is
explain: Comparing the bending deflection (from flexure formula) to the axial elongation e of the same circular bar under the same load W gives a deflection expression proportional to e²l/3d², matching option (c).

q: 14. A cantilever of length L is subjected to a bending moment M at its free end. If EI is the flexural rigidity of the section, the deflection of the free end is
explain: For a cantilever under a pure end moment M, standard deflection formula gives free-end deflection = ML²/2EI.

q: 15. The maximum bending moment for a simply supported beam with a uniformly distributed load w/unit length is
explain: For a simply supported beam under UDL w per unit length, the maximum bending moment (at midspan) is wl²/8, a standard result.

q: 16. A simply supported beam carries a varying load from zero at one end to w at the other end. If the length of the beam is a, the shear force will be zero at a distance x from least loaded point where x is
explain: For a triangularly (linearly) varying load, the shear force becomes zero at x = a/√3 measured from the zero-load end, a standard result for such loading.

q: 17. Along the neutral axis of a simply supported beam
explain: By definition, the neutral axis is the layer where bending stress and strain are zero.

q: 18. A simply supported beam carries varying load from zero at one end and w at the other end, the length of the beam is a, the maximum bending moment will be
explain: For a linearly varying load, maximum bending moment occurs at x=a/√3 from the zero-load end and evaluates to Wa²/(9√3), the standard closed-form result.

q: 19. The load on spring per unit deflection is called
explain: Stiffness is defined as the load required to produce unit deflection in a spring (k = W/δ).

q: 20. The algebraic sum of the vertical forces on either side of the section of a loaded beam is known as
explain: Shear force at any section is the net vertical force acting on one side of that section.

q: 21. Find the shear force produced in the member BC due to load shown in fig.
explain: Based on the figure, the vertical load applied at C is 4 kN, which remains constant through the member BC.

q: 22. Find the bending moment at fixed end of cantilever as shown in fig.
explain: The moment is calculated by the sum of forces times their distances (5T × 2m + 10 Tm = 20 Tm).

q: 23. A portion of beam between two sections is said to be in pure bending when there is
options: constant bending moment and zero shear force
constant shear force and zero bending moment
constant bending moment and constant shear force
explain: Pure bending occurs over a beam segment where the bending moment is constant and the shear force is zero (since dM/dx = V = 0 implies M is constant).

q: 24. Of the several prismatic beams of equal lengths, the strongest in flexure is one having the maximum
explain: Bending strength (moment carrying capacity for a given allowable stress) is M = σ×Z, so the beam with maximum section modulus Z is the strongest in flexure.

q: 25. A rectangular beam carries a maximum bending moment of M. If its depth is doubled, its moment carrying capacity will be
explain: Moment capacity is proportional to the Section Modulus Z (BD²/6). If D is doubled (2D), Z becomes B(2D)²/6 = 4BD²/6, increasing capacity 4 times.

q: 26. A prismatic bar when subjected to pure bending assumes the shape of
explain: Under pure (constant) bending moment, curvature 1/R = M/EI is constant, so the beam bends into a circular arc.

q: 27. The algebraic sum of the moments of the forces on either side of the section of a loaded beam is known as
explain: This is the formal definition of the internal bending moment at a specific point in a beam.

q: 28. The shear force and bending moment are related by
explain: The rate of change of the bending moment (dM/dx) at any section is equal to the shear force (V) at that section.

q: 29. A beam of uniform strength has at every cross section same
explain: A beam of uniform strength is designed such that the maximum bending stress is the same (equal to allowable stress) at every cross-section, even though the moment and dimensions vary.

q: 30. The shear force on a beam and the displacement are related by
explain: Bending Moment M = EI(d²y/dx²). Since V = dM/dx, it follows that V = EI(d³y/dx³).

q: 31. Which one is correct if the deflection of a beam is y
explain: The slope (θ) of a beam's elastic curve is the first derivative of the deflection (y) with respect to x.

q: 32. Two beams one of circular cross section and other of square cross section have equal area of cross section. If subjected to bending
explain: For equal cross-sectional area, a square section has a greater section modulus than a circular one, making the square section more economical (stronger) in bending.

q: 33. Calculate the maximum BM introduced due to a udl of 4KN/m, if the span of the cantilever is 1.8m
explain: Maximum BM for a cantilever with UDL is wL²/2. (4 × 1.8²) / 2 = 6.48 KN-M.

q: 34. Find the bending moment at 1/4th of the span having simply supported beam with following data: point load = 200 kg at centre, span = 20m
explain: Reaction at support is 100 kg. At x = 5m (1/4th span), BM = 100 kg × 5m = 500 kg-m.

q: 35. The maximum deflection in the cantilever beam subjected to an udl of W /m throughout the span is
explain: This is a standard deflection formula for a cantilever beam under a uniformly distributed load.

q: 36. A simply supported beam of length l carries a load varying uniformly from zero at left end to maximum at right end maximum bending moment occurs at a distance of
explain: For a triangular load, the maximum moment occurs where shear force is zero, which is at a distance of l/√3 from the apex (zero load end).

q: 37. Load carrying capacity of fixed beam is
options: greater than simply supported beam and cantilever beam
explain: A fixed beam has a higher degree of redundancy and smaller maximum bending moments compared to simply supported or cantilever beams for the same span and loading, allowing it to carry more load.

q: 38. The difference in placing the end of a beam simply over a support and the supporting end through a hinge on rollers is that the roller support
options: can offer reaction in the plane of rollers
will not allowed the end to lift up the deflection
will not offer reaction normal to the plane of rollers
explain: A roller support allows horizontal movement and rotation but constrains vertical movement; however, in standard civil engineering contexts, it prevents the beam from lifting off the support surface.

q: 39. At either ends of plane frame, maximum number of possible bending moment, are
explain: According to the provided answer key, the value is zero; this typically refers to idealized hinged or pinned connections at the ends of a frame where no moment is transferred.

q: 40. A simply supported beam of span L carries a uniformly distributed load, w. The maximum shear force, V is
explain: For a simply supported beam with UDL, the total load is wL. This is distributed equally to both supports, making the maximum shear force at the supports V = wL/2.

q: 41. A simply supported beam of span L carries a uniformly distributed load, w. The maximum bending moment, M is
explain: The maximum bending moment for a simply supported beam with a UDL occurs at the center and is calculated as M = wL²/8.

q: 42. A simply supported beam of span L carries two equal concentrated loads, W at a distance of L/3 from either support. The maximum bending moment, M is
explain: The reaction at each support is W. The maximum moment occurs between the two loads and is equal to Reaction × Distance = W × (L/3).

q: 43. A beam is hinged at both ends and loaded with a triangular load having maximum intensity (W) at centre. Find the maximum bending moment & shear force
explain: For a triangular load (reaching peak W at center) on a simply supported span L, the total load is WL/2, the reactions are WL/4, and the peak moment at the center is WL²/12.

q: 44. The shape of bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, having no external load is
explain: When there is no external load (only point loads or moments at ends), the shear force is constant and the bending moment varies linearly.

q: 45. The shape of bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, carrying a uniformly distributed load is
explain: The bending moment is the integral of the shear force. For a UDL, the shear force is linear, so the bending moment diagram follows a second-degree (parabolic) curve.

q: 46. In any beam, there is acting uniformly moment then its curve is
explain: The key indicates 'parabolic arch', though pure bending (constant moment) typically results in a circular elastic curve; however, in the context of load diagrams, 'parabolic' is often associated with distributed forces.

q: 47. If the length of a cantilever carrying an isolated load at its free end is doubled, the deflection of the free end will increase by
explain: Cantilever tip deflection δ = WL³/3EI is proportional to L³; doubling L increases deflection by a factor of 2³ = 8.

q: 48. The shape of bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, carrying a uniformly increasing load is
explain: A uniformly increasing load (triangular) results in a parabolic shear force (2nd degree) and a cubical bending moment diagram (3rd degree).

q: 49. If the width of a simply supported beam carrying an isolated load at its centre is doubled, deflection of the beam at the centre is changed by
explain: Deflection δ ∝ 1/I ∝ 1/b (for rectangular section, I ∝ b); doubling width b halves the deflection.

q: 50. The maximum bending moment due to moving load on a simply supported beam occurs
explain: For a single moving point load on a simply supported beam, the maximum bending moment always occurs directly under the load position.
